$comment: The complete vocabulary of the Build surface. Adding a dimension here, with a derive block, is the only way to extend it. No count is fixed: manifest.json lists which dimensions are live in each build (docs/CUBE_SCHEMA.md). derive kinds are documented in pipeline/derive.py; fields are the logical names bound in config/pipeline.json. Every dimension states its kind (category, ordered_band or place) and its cardinality; the chart rules read them (config/chart_rules.json).

dimensions.label: Powertrain
dimensions.public_note: NZTA does not record whether a hybrid is mild or full. Mild hybrids are picked out by model name, so the mild hybrid line counts only the ones identified; the note below says what share that is.
dimensions.$note_condition_comment: Both notes speak of a mild hybrid line. A dataset that does not divide its hybrids (manifest: mild_split_published false) has none, so the notes read as the _otherwise ones say; the chart then carries the sentence defaults.phrases.mild_split_withheld. The conditions are listed in src/lib/dimensionNote.ts.
dimensions.public_note_otherwise: NZTA does not record whether a hybrid is mild or full.
dimensions.note_otherwise: NZTA does not record whether a hybrid is mild or full. This dataset does not divide its hybrids (mild_split_published is false), so they are one value and there is no mild line to relabel.
dimensions.help: How the vehicle is powered: petrol, diesel, hybrid, plug-in hybrid, electric.
dimensions.note: NZTA does not record whether a hybrid is mild or full. Mild hybrids are identified by nameplate, so the category takes the label and coverage published in the manifest (mild_hybrid_identification_coverage): 'Mild hybrid (identified)' with its coverage, until coverage is high.

dimensions.label: Brand
dimensions.help: The badge on the car. Normalised via the brand registry.

dimensions.label: Manufacturer group
dimensions.$cardinality_comment: high, like make: 43 named groups in the 2026-08 cube, every one with vehicles in the last 12 months, the 14 largest holding 88% of those vehicles. A single 12-month window of competitors is drawn as a ranking (league), as for brands; longer periods stay a mix chart (D-050).
dimensions.help: Who owns the brand. Toyota, Lexus and Daihatsu all roll up to Toyota Group.

dimensions.label: Brand owned from
dimensions.help: The home country of the company that owns the brand today, or for a defunct brand the last company that built it. Volvo counts as China here.

dimensions.label: Brand originally from
dimensions.help: Where the brand was founded. Volvo counts as Sweden here.

dimensions.label: Built in
dimensions.public_note: Where a vehicle was built is not recorded for almost every vehicle first registered before late 1985, and is recorded for almost all since. The grey line near the top of the chart until then is that gap in the record, not where vehicles came from.
dimensions.help: The country where the vehicle was principally manufactured. A Toyota built in Thailand counts as Thailand.

dimensions.label: Imported from
dimensions.help: Where a used import was registered before coming to NZ.

dimensions.label: Vehicle type
dimensions.help: Car, ute, van, truck or other. The register records most SUVs as station wagons, so they count as cars.
dimensions.$comment: segment_map matches on vehicle_type + body_type. Where gvm_min_kg/gvm_max_kg are set, GVM must fall in that inclusive range and a missing GVM matches nothing; where both are blank, GVM is not used.

dimensions.label: Vehicle class
dimensions.help: Light passenger, light commercial, heavy commercial or other, from the same vehicle type, body and gross vehicle mass as vehicle type. Not the same split: utes and vans fall in all three classes.
dimensions.$comment: The same segment_map.csv match as segment, reading its segment_group column, so powertrain-mix can narrow to light passenger vehicles. segment = Car is not light passenger: light passenger also holds the passenger-registered utes and vans.

dimensions.label: Registered as
dimensions.public_note: The type NZTA registers the vehicle under. It is a different thing from Vehicle type, which sorts vehicles into cars, utes, vans and trucks from the body and weight as well: a ute can be registered as a passenger vehicle. Only the types this site counts are shown.
dimensions.help: The type NZTA registers the vehicle under, such as passenger cars and vans. It is not the car, ute, van and truck split of Vehicle type, which also reads the body type and weight.
dimensions.$comment: The lookup reads the same vehicle_scope.csv key that decides which vehicles are in scope, so it cannot meet a type that scope does not know (the build aborts on one). Only in-scope types reach a slice; a type brought into scope later appears under its label with no other change. A series source carries no register field, so the dimension is not live for registrations_cars_long_run (derive.applicable), with no applies_to.

dimensions.label: Passenger or commercial
dimensions.public_note: Passenger vehicles are the vehicles NZTA registers as passenger cars and vans. Commercial is every other type this dataset counts: goods vans, trucks and utes, buses, motor caravans and special purpose vehicles. It follows the type a vehicle is registered under, so a ute registered as a passenger vehicle is a passenger vehicle here.
dimensions.help: Whether the vehicle is registered as a passenger car or van, or as one of the other types the wider scope counts. Commercial here is every counted type but passenger.
dimensions.$comment: The same vehicle_scope.csv key as vehicle_type, reading the trade_group column the file gives each type of its wider scope. A type outside that scope has no group and never reaches this dataset. The dataset is the only one that names it: registrations_flow counts the same two groups' vehicles of the default scope, and offering the dimension there would add a file to a dataset this work leaves as it was (D-113).

dimensions.label: New or used
dimensions.help: Whether the vehicle was new or second-hand when it first entered NZ.

dimensions.label: New or ex-overseas
dimensions.public_note: New cars are Stats NZ's total less the cars previously registered overseas.
dimensions.source: statsnz:cars total + statsnz:cars previously registered overseas + reference:import_status_map
dimensions.help: Whether the car was new when it entered NZ or had been registered overseas first, as Stats NZ counts them. The two values carry the same names as new or used on the other datasets, so they can be set side by side.

dimensions.label: Engine size (Stats NZ bands)
dimensions.public_note: The bands cover new and ex-overseas cars together.
dimensions.source: statsnz:cars by engine size (seven bands) + reference:statsnz_series
dimensions.help: Engine size in the seven bands Stats NZ uses, from up to 850 cc to 5001 cc and over. These are not the engine size bands of the other datasets.

dimensions.label: Region
dimensions.help: The region where the registered owner lives now, from their most recent address. Not where the vehicle is used, and not necessarily where the owner lived when it was first registered.

dimensions.label: Vehicle age
dimensions.public_note: Age on the snapshot date, not when the vehicle was bought. It is counted from the year NZTA records for each vehicle, not from when it was built: for a vehicle sold new here since 2007, the year it was first registered here; for a used import, a year from its life overseas, usually when it was built or first registered there. For vehicles sold new here before 2007 that year is less consistent, sometimes a year early. A year, not a date, so an age can be out by a year.
dimensions.help: Years since the vehicle year. For NZ-new vehicles first registered from 2007 that is years since first registration; for used imports, years since the vehicle's year overseas. Vehicle year is less consistent for NZ-new vehicles registered before 2007.
dimensions.$comment: min and max are inclusive; max null means no upper bound. A missing VEHICLE_YEAR, a VEHICLE_YEAR of 0, or a negative result (vehicle years after the snapshot exist) falls to unknown.

dimensions.label: Engine size
dimensions.help: Engine capacity in bands. Electric vehicles fall in a separate 'none' band.
dimensions.basis: CC_RATING, for powertrains with has_combustion_engine = true in powertrain_map
dimensions.$comment: min and max are inclusive cc; max null means no upper bound. A powertrain without a combustion engine is 'none' whatever CC_RATING says (14% of BEVs record a small non-zero CC). An engined vehicle whose CC is missing or below the lowest min (0, and implausible values such as 1 or 19 cc that appear in the data) is unknown.

dimensions.label: Age when first registered here
dimensions.public_note: Age when first registered in New Zealand, counted from the year NZTA records for each vehicle. A vehicle sold new here since 2007 is 0 years old by definition, because that year is its first registration here; for a used import it is a year from its life overseas, usually when it was built or first registered there. For vehicles sold new here before 2007 that year is less consistent, sometimes a year early. A year, not a date, so an age can be out by a year. Counted among vehicles still registered at the snapshot: arrivals from earlier years have had longer to leave the register, and vehicles do not all leave at the same rate, so the longer the span, the more the ages shown may differ from those that arrived at the time.
dimensions.help: How old the vehicle was when it was first registered in New Zealand. Zero means new.
dimensions.$comment: min and max are inclusive years; max null means no upper bound. Single years to 19 because the moving cutoff and odd-age bumps are one year wide (MODEL_AND_AGE.md section 3). A missing VEHICLE_YEAR, a VEHICLE_YEAR of 0 and a negative result each fall to unknown and are counted separately in the manifest (MODEL_AND_AGE.md section 5).

dimensions.label: Imported or assembled here
dimensions.public_note: NZTA's flag for whether a vehicle was assembled or built in New Zealand or imported built up. It is a flag, not a place: a vehicle assembled here from an imported kit records the kit's country as where it was built. Recording starts in late 1995, so vehicles first registered before then show as not recorded, and the grey line near the top of the chart until then is that gap in the record. Very few vehicles first registered in recent years are marked as assembled here, so their figures rest on small counts.
dimensions.help: Whether NZTA records the vehicle as imported built up or as assembled or built in New Zealand. Not where it was built: see Built in.
dimensions.$comment: UNKNOWN is a sentinel (sentinels.csv), so it reads as not recorded; a new raw value has no row in nz_assembled_map.csv and trips the unmapped guard (pipeline.json guardrails.abort_on_unmapped). A series source carries no register field, so the dimension is not live for registrations_cars_long_run, and the dashboard export has none, so it is not live for the two flow datasets (derive.applicable), with no applies_to.

dimensions.label: NZTA class code
dimensions.public_note: NZTA's vehicle equipment standard class, shown as its code. Recording is patchy before 2002 and differs between new and used vehicles, so the mix of classes before then, and the vehicles with no class recorded, show what was recorded, not what was registered. NA is a class of light goods vehicle, not a missing value. A class sits under one type of vehicle, so setting the two side by side shows the same split twice.
dimensions.help: NZTA's vehicle equipment standard class, as its code. What each code means has not been read from NZTA's or the Land Transport Rules' definitions, so the codes are shown as they are.
dimensions.$comment: A blank class is the only form of not recorded: it reads __UNDEFINED__ and sentinels.csv lists none for this field, because NA is a real class (a light goods vehicle) and must never be treated as one. class_map.csv holds every code on the whole register, so a vehicle type brought into scope later does not trip the unmapped guard, and a new code does (pipeline.json guardrails.abort_on_unmapped). Not live for the datasets whose source carries no class (derive.applicable), with no applies_to.

dimensions.label: Seats
dimensions.public_note: The number of seats NZTA records, in bands. Seats are not recorded for many of the vehicles first registered from early 1994 to late 1995, so unknown is large for those months and small otherwise. A count of zero is not recorded, and a count above 60 is not taken as a number of seats: both are counted as unknown.
dimensions.help: How many seats NZTA records for the vehicle, in bands from 1-2 to 8 or more.
dimensions.basis: NUMBER_OF_SEATS, inside the guard of 1 to 60
dimensions.$comment: min and max are inclusive; the top band stops at the guard (60), so a count above it, which is not a number of seats, falls to unknown. A zero is the form of not recorded (sentinels.csv), so it is NULL by the time it is banded and falls to unknown too; the manifest counts the two causes apart (bands.seats_band.source_sentinel, out_of_bands). No mean or median is built.

dimensions.label: Model
dimensions.help: The nameplate, as brand and model. Only the models with the most vehicles over the trailing 12 months, counted as the dataset counts them, keep their name; the rest are grouped as other. The cap is in this dimension's derive block and every build publishes it. Never use submodel, which is free text.
dimensions.note_template: Only the {dataset.model_cap.model.cap} models with the most {words.cap_count} in the trailing {dataset.coverage_trailing.window_months} months are named, so older months are mostly grouped as other and historical coverage is partial. Named models cover {dataset.model_cap.model.coverage_trailing|pct} of trailing volume and {dataset.model_cap.model.coverage_all_time|pct} of all-time volume.

periods.label: All time
periods.$comment: No months: runs from the dataset's first month to the latest snapshot.

rules.$comment: Shape is inferred from measure + dimension. See CLAUDE.md Shapes. There is no limit on the number of conditions a question carries (D-062, D-107): a key that said two was read by nothing and was removed.
